statement: Cards are laid out in a row; cardPoints[i] is the number of points card i is worth.
You take exactly k cards, one at a time, and each card must come from the left end or the right end of what remains. Your score is the total of the cards you take.

Return the highest possible score. Whatever you take, the cards left behind form one contiguous block of n − k cards, so you can equally try every split of i cards from the left and k − i from the right and keep the best sum.

examples.explanation: Taking the three rightmost cards, 1, 6 and 5, scores 12. Any choice that uses a card from the left end gives less.
Both ends are 9s. Taking the first and the last card scores 18; taking two from the same end gives only 16.
